title: The Letter of Peace, the Kingdoms, the Four Works of Sin
description: The conversation between Lord and soul, set against the kingdoms of the world and the works of self-love. T76 — the Apostle's "peace and greeting" as the letter between Call and Hearing: the conversation between the Lord's summons and the soul's answer, in which everything that has come to pass between them is set down, ascending with the rational when it rises home. T77 — the four kingdoms in the natural mind, none exalted exceedingly above the others; every dominion that organizes itself within the natural stands only at its own degree. T78 — the four great works of self-love (appetite of the mouth, disorder of joining, love of possession, lust for dominion) met by the single saving work: the separation of the beautiful from the bad, established forth in obedience.
